scope: Rapid evidence screen, no hardware/native/task implementation. PASS FOR DEEP DIVE is not category qualification or GPU readiness.

rows.operation: Release the actual retaining clips and remove the front door trim without bending/marring it, as access for power-window motor service.
rows.equipment: 2013 U.S. Hyundai Elantra L4-1.8L front door trim/panel, actual matching retaining clips, ordinary plastic panel-removal tool; exact clip/tool part numbers still to bind.

procedure_sources.provenance: Exact vehicle-specific Operation CHARM workshop reproduction read in pinned third-party archive. Original OEM publication and matching service-part numbers not independently authenticated.
Exact vehicle-specific Operation CHARM workshop reproduction read in pinned third-party archive. Original OEM publication and matching service-part numbers not independently authenticated.

rows.procedure_verified: READ: exact trim and power-window-motor service sequence in CHARM reproduction; no OEM-origin hash match.

core_duty.employment_source: MIT-WAL pinned May2025 OEWS export, national row; third-party mirror, not live BLS
core_duty.task: Install, adjust, or repair hydraulic or electromagnetic automatic lift mechanisms used to raise and lower automobile windows, seats, and tops.
core_duty.bridge: Page863 names front-door trim removal as first step of power-window motor replacement. This grounds trim access in an explicit Core repair, rather than claiming every cosmetic clip job qualifies.

comparators.operation: Refit splash shield by aligning holes and installing a push-in retaining clip
comparators.distinction: Installation/capture of a loose clip through two holes versus controlled release of retained clips from an actual panel; same component class requires semantic scope comparison, not automatic duplication.

comparators.operation: Back up spring-loaded trim panel while pressing fake plunger
comparators.distinction: Review explicitly says no retaining fastener and rigid sprung plate; cannot use its shortcuts as precedent. Its old simulator-state expert objection is superseded by Version21.

comparators.operation: Extract fuse with tong puller, rock and recover
comparators.distinction: Tool-assisted extraction overlaps force control, but electrical fuse friction/extraction has a different retaining interface than releasing vehicle trim clips.

rows.new_manipulation: Find an accessible trim-clip load path and insert/pry with a real panel tool while supporting a compliant real panel; release clip capture without replacing it by a plunger or unsupported lever rule.
rows.physical_success: Actual clips disengaged and bounded trim section/panel removable under ordinary handling; no broken retaining seats, new visible marring or permanent panel bend beyond a justified measured baseline. Use before/after photos, straightedge and actual clip/seat inspection; recovered clips need not be reusable if OEM calls for replacement. Do not score only distance moved.
rows.complexity: Medium/high: bounded panel/clip compliance and pry-tool contact; full-door perimeter may add substantial reach and multiple fasteners. A disclosed physically calibrated local clip/panel model can be adequate; no full textile model needed.
rows.YAM_obstacle: Stock tool grip, wedge access next to door flange, panel reaction and tool sweep. Use real accessible clip/panel geometry and an honest bounded service start; do not shrink a whole door or add a fake grip post.
rows.strongest_reviewer_objection: Ordinary clip extraction presented as an important job without preserving panel/access mechanics, or an inverse/component variant of #1986. The narrow scope must retain meaningful clip-release skill rather than just prying a loose plate.
missing_evidence: Exact clip/seat and permitted tool dimensions/materials
Meaningful retained release scoring tolerance and damage baseline
Origin-aware current comparison to #1986 and external suites
Real force and stock-gripper swept access before implementation
rows.cheap_kill: First photograph/measure an actual compatible clip seat and plastic tool at 1:1 and inspect whether full fingertips/palm can reach without deleting door features; then hand-rehearse clip release and wrong-position pry negative if genuine hardware is available. No test performed.

rows.operation: Separate the genuinely seated outer tie-rod taper from a steering knuckle using the correct screw-type separator.
rows.equipment: Candidate: 2013 Elantra outer tie rod/knuckle plus matching screw separator; OTC model only a search lead, not selected or verified.

procedure_sources.provenance: Exact vehicle-specific Operation CHARM workshop reproduction read in pinned third-party archive. Original OEM publication and matching service-part numbers not independently authenticated.
Exact vehicle-specific Operation CHARM workshop reproduction read in pinned third-party archive. Original OEM publication and matching service-part numbers not independently authenticated.

rows.procedure_verified: PARTIAL: exact vehicle source verifies removal of tie-rod end after split pin/castle nut, but does NOT prescribe an OTC screw separator or its safe seating/load/release method.

core_duty.task: Tear down, repair, and rebuild faulty assemblies, such as power systems, steering systems, and linkages.
core_duty.bridge: Exact source places tie-rod end removal inside front hub/knuckle and steering-gear service. Tool-specific method remains unverified.

comparators.operation: Seat swivelling tie-rod ball stud into tapered knuckle hole
comparators.distinction: Same real objects/setting, but acquiring a separator to break a preloaded taper has different load path and endpoint from seating an unpreloaded ball stud. Needs actual source-backed preload/tool mechanics, not just inverse-motion claim.

comparators.operation: Extract interference collar using already-prepared two-jaw screw puller
comparators.distinction: Same screw-to-axial-force principle; taper separator must seat reaction surfaces on real knuckle/stud and cause physical taper release, not become another prepared screw extraction.

comparators.operation: Drive bearing onto shaft through selected ring using sleeve
comparators.distinction: Review rejected a rule-choice-plus-prealigned press. N042 cannot rely on choosing the correct illustrated tool as its main difficulty.

rows.new_manipulation: Seat fork/reaction jaw and screw tip on an actual loaded taper assembly, retain alignment while generating separation force and manage released joint.
rows.physical_success: Real taper disengaged, stud free from matched knuckle seat, separator and joint retained without damaged boot/thread/seat; independent manual movement/visible separation after unloading. Screw rotations alone are not success.
rows.complexity: Medium/high unknown: screw mechanics are bounded, but force buildup, compliance, contact shift and sudden release must be genuine. Not estimated from rigid-part count.
rows.YAM_obstacle: Real separator size/jaw opening, screw torque transfer, release transient, and access around boot/castle-nut/stud. No numeric required torque currently verified.
rows.strongest_reviewer_objection: A generic low-force peg pop is substituted for separating a real loaded taper, or this merely reverses #914/duplicates prepared screw extraction #369 without new tool acquisition.
missing_evidence: Read exact compatible separator OEM instructions
Actual tie-rod/knuckle application and preload/reaction method
Boundary comparison to #914 and #369 current ownership
Stock-grip tool torque and release access
rows.cheap_kill: Bind a genuine separator and verify its actual jaw/reaction placement and force on a real matched joint before any scene work. If the job only fits after weakening the taper or presetting the tool, stop.

rows.operation: Acquire and fit a genuine two-jaw puller to a bearing on a shaft, then extract it without losing jaw engagement.
rows.equipment: Posi Lock two-jaw family remains a search target; no exact OEM puller/bearing/SKU combination verified. The inspected Elantra wheel-bearing operation uses a press and adapters, not this puller.

procedure_sources.provenance: Exact vehicle-specific Operation CHARM workshop reproduction read in pinned third-party archive. Original OEM publication and matching service-part numbers not independently authenticated.

rows.procedure_verified: MISMATCH FOUND: readable matched vehicle procedure is press-based and cannot substantiate the proposed two-jaw extraction. Posi Lock exact instructions not obtained.

core_duty.task: Repair or replace parts such as pistons, rods, gears, valves, and bearings.
core_duty.bridge: Bearing work is directly Core; this does not select or validate a two-jaw procedure where the read manual calls for press/support adapters.

comparators.operation: Prepared two-jaw screw puller extracts fitted collar
comparators.distinction: Explicitly starts with hooks pre-engaged, excluding fitting the puller. Proper multi-contact jaw acquisition could be a meaningful additional skill, but actual puller setup and centrality require proof; not automatically duplicate because both turn a screw.

comparators.operation: Bearing installation with inner-ring force sleeve
comparators.distinction: Different direction/tool interface, but selecting the correct force ring alone is not sufficient robotic difficulty.

comparators.operation: Seat ball stud in matched tapered hole
comparators.distinction: Interference/taper engagement is related, not a bearing-puller extraction endpoint.

rows.new_manipulation: Center screw on shaft while fitting two real jaws behind bearing shoulder; maintain all reaction contacts as interference releases. Must not start with pre-engaged jaws.
rows.physical_success: Bearing actually clears shaft while remaining safely controlled; shaft/bearing load surfaces not damaged by wrong ring/jaw placement. Independent released bearing position and genuine fit failure controls, not turns-to-position latch.
rows.complexity: High/uncertain force/contact: multi-contact jaw seating, screw friction, retained reaction, bearing interference and release. Large real puller loads may exceed stock tool grip.
rows.YAM_obstacle: Access behind bearing, jaw reach and small shoulder clearance, stabilizing puller while starting screw, required torque and real part/tool mass.
rows.strongest_reviewer_objection: A different pulled collar called a bearing duplicates active #369, with the task core already prepared; or a read press-based OEM job is falsely presented as approving a jaw puller.
missing_evidence: Readable exact puller OEM procedure and compatible real job
Actual bearing shoulder/shaft support and force requirements
Decide whether non-prepared puller fitting is meaningful and independent of #369
Current ownership and genuine grasp/reaction access
rows.cheap_kill: First source-select a real job that permits this exact puller. If only an unrelated press procedure is available, do not substitute the tool. Then map jaws and stock fingertips at real shoulder clearance and calculate required force/torque from measured fit.

rows.operation: Wrap and secure a genuine cushioned P-clamp around a supported hydraulic hose and fasten its ears to the real mounting tab.
rows.equipment: Adel/MS21919-style cushioned P-clamp was a bank equipment lead only. No exact clamp/hose/mount OEM installation procedure was read.
rows.procedure_verified: NO exact read procedure. Elantra sources inspected for line/hose service do not establish the bank’s cushioned P-clamp installation.

core_duty.occupation: 49-3023.00 Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics (candidate only)
core_duty.task: Repair and service air conditioning, heating, engine cooling, and electrical systems.
core_duty.bridge: Related hose-bearing systems are Core, but exact cushioned P-clamp routine and compatible service application are not established. Do not borrow aircraft employment or all mechanics for an unbound aviation clamp.

comparators.operation: Install split cable guide around connected service-drawer cable and test travel
comparators.distinction: Wrapping around a connected flexible member is shared; actual cushioned restraint and matched ear bolt could differ, but a clamp variant needs real functional support.

comparators.operation: Lay motor/encoder cable in igus carrier and close crossbars
comparators.distinction: Protecting routed flexible members and closing catches overlaps, but fixed P-clamp strain relief is a different interface if authentic.

comparators.operation: Torque busbar lug bolt with click-type wrench
comparators.distinction: Bolted tightening shared; fastener torque alone does not supply P-clamp novelty or hose protection.

rows.new_manipulation: Control sprung clamp ears around a real flexible hose while obtaining bolt alignment without pinching/displacing its cushion; no fictional collar latch.
rows.physical_success: Real clamp fully surrounds hose with cushion correctly placed, genuine ears/bolt seated on mounting tab, hose retained without specified pinch/kink under a justified benign check. Numeric torque/slip limits need actual source.
rows.complexity: Medium/high unknown: bounded sprung metal and cushion compliance plus flexible hose reaction and thread acquisition. Not low simply because few parts.
rows.YAM_obstacle: Compressing/seating sprung ears while starting a small bolt, accessing rear of mounting tab, avoiding hose crush with stock fingers.
rows.strongest_reviewer_objection: An unsupported niche clamp operation inherits general maintenance employment; a generic strap/bolt replaces the genuine cushion/ear interface, or duplicates the accepted split-guide assembly in substance.
missing_evidence: Read exact compatible clamp/hose installation instructions
Direct routine duty-to-application bridge for a qualifying occupation
Real ear spring load, clamp size and tool access
rows.cheap_kill: Obtain a real documented application before CAD. If only aircraft usage or generic clamp catalogue pictures support the idea, do not claim a qualifying jobs case; map genuine ear/bolt/tool access once selected.

comments: Bimanual task: one arm backs a spring-seated panel from underneath with a fork paddle (sag <= 3 mm) while the other arm presses a detent clip into it, then withdraws. Scripted demo scores 1.0 in simulation; ablations (press only, back only) score 0.25 and 0.5; Dream-1 run scored 0.0. README lists deviations (no latch, softer springs).

Not accepted: final (TK-F3VZB7). Flags: Egregious simplification Importance (not met): The stated automotive relevance rests on calling a spring-loaded button a trim clip, although the specified build does not install or retain a fastener. Construct validity (not met): The specified real-world build uses an unlatched plunger and rigid spring-mounted panel instead of a retaining clip and a flexing trim panel. Scoring (not met): The implementation awards 0.75 after one qualifying step and can report 1.0 before the required stillness hold, contrary to the stated scoring. Clarity and reproducibility (not met): The real-world setup omits material specifications and enough dimensions for the fork, grip post, base and spring seats to reproduce the fixture. Feasibility (not met): The scripted demo controls its actions using exact simulator object poses and clip-slider travel rather than robot-observable measurements. The proposed fixture replaces clip installation with pressing a spring-return plunger, and replaces a flexing trim panel with a rigid plate on springs. It therefore does not represent the claimed fastening and panel-protection skill; a real retaining clip and representative panel assembly would constitute a different task. The scripted demo also relies on simulator-internal object poses and clip travel, and the scorer's hold-time behavior does not match the documented thresholds. If you think this misjudges your task, reply on this pull request within 48 hours and a person will review it. This task doesn’t meet the importance bar, so it can’t be revised, and this pull request is now closed. You’re welcome to submit a different task in a new pull request.
